requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: etcd v3.5.17 installed and configured on all three nodes with static bootstrap; endpoint health for all three endpoints returns true and member list shows all three (node1/node2/node3) in 'started' state.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: Key 'testkey' written via node1's endpoint was successfully read back with identical value from node2's and node3's endpoints.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped (bounded, reversible disruption), a new key was written via node1 and read via node2 while node3 remained down, and endpoint health for the two remaining members was true throughout.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted; it successfully served the key written during its outage and endpoint health/status showed it rejoined the 3/3 healthy cluster with a consistent raft applied index, directly demonstrating the recovery transition (down -> restored -> caught up).

overall_summary: The executor built a working 3-member etcd cluster on node1/node2/node3, with direct evidence of cross-member read/write consistency, continued read/write availability while node3 was stopped, and node3 catching up and rejoining the healthy cluster after restart -- satisfying all material outcomes of the task contract with concrete before/during/after command evidence rather than configuration alone. The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also executed and documented for all three nodes with matching pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot_id, and post-restart health/data/quorum recovery, and this is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare vs after_executor) for all three nodes. The only notable imperfection is leftover install/download artifacts (tarball, extracted directory, reboot log) left in /tmp on each node, a minor, low-risk hygiene issue rather than a functional deficiency.
limitations: No independent (non-executor-reported) confirmation exists that the etcd data survived the full sequential three-node reboot sequence beyond the executor's own etcdctl reads (testkey/keywhilenode3down) captured after each reboot; these are treated as direct evidence since they are terminal command outputs, but there is no separately captured system-level data integrity check.

The prepare phase was disabled/static and identical to before_prepare, so no preparer-created state needed to be distinguished from executor changes; all observed deltas are attributable to the executor.

Command timeline shows one failed first bootstrap attempt on node1 (cmd-fe11e64fbf03484f, timeout) that was immediately retried and succeeded; this is treated as a corrective action, not a task failure, consistent with observed final healthy state.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: binary installation, etcd user/data dir creation, static config and unit files, firewalld port openings (necessary for cluster function), the reboot protocol, and one corrective retry of a failed node1 bootstrap attempt (no evidence of harm, immediately fixed). The main hygiene gap is leftover build artifacts on all three nodes -- /tmp/etcd.tar.gz, the extracted /tmp/etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, and /tmp/reboot.log -- visible in the after_executor snapshot on node1/node2/node3 and never cleaned up (introduced by cmd-3763e6934ed94fb4/cmd-f63622ecc07d441c/cmd-92ba3399e98343eb download and cmd-51f6cc2db3724f10/cmd-e03162be22c549ea/cmd-e467f54fff3b488a extraction, and by the reboot-scheduling commands). These are low-risk, non-destructive residue (temp install artifacts, not secrets or config), so this is treated as a minor deduction rather than a serious violation. No failed services, no unsafe exposure changes beyond the ports required for etcd's own peer/client communication, and no damaged package state were observed.
